title: Sunny and the Little Turtle | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka meets a tiny freshwater turtle resting on a moonlit rock, and together they share the quietest, most peaceful moment in the whole bush. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The rock was small and flat and perfectly placed — right at the edge of the creek where the moonlight fell just so.

And on that rock sat a turtle.

She was tiny. Her shell was dark and smooth, the colour of wet river stones. Her eyes were very old-looking for such a small creature — round and still and quiet.

Little Sunny the quokka crept closer, very slowly, so as not to startle her.

The turtle did not move.

Sunny sat down on the bank beside the rock and looked at the turtle. The turtle looked at Sunny.

Neither of them said anything. There was nothing that needed saying.

The creek made a soft sound as it passed around the rock — a low, continuous murmur, like someone telling a very long, very quiet story.

The moon moved a little higher. Its light spread across the water in long silver ribbons.

The turtle blinked — very slowly — and her eyes closed halfway.

Sunny blinked too.

They stayed like that for a long while. Two small creatures, sitting together in the moonlight, listening to the creek, not hurrying anywhere at all.

The turtle's head lowered. Just a little.

Sunny felt her own eyes growing heavy.

The creek kept murmuring its long, quiet story.

And they both drifted off, side by side, into the softest sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little turtle. Goodnight, little one.
